title: Gradient Descent Field Notes — Human + AI Learning Notebook

source.html:
Notebook 01 · Concept

Gradient descent, by feel.

A three-minute mental model for finding the bottom of a curve—without memorizing the machinery first.

The one idea

Look at the slope. Step downhill.

xnew=xold−η×slope
  1. Measure direction: the slope says which way is uphill.
  2. Reverse it: subtracting the slope points downhill.
  3. Choose stride: η controls how bold the step is.

AI study partner

Use a hiking metaphor.

If your boots tilt upward to the right, walk left. If the ground is nearly flat, you are probably close to the valley floor.

Prediction checkpoint

For loss L(x) = (x − 3)², you stand at x = −4. Which way is the minimum?

Choose the direction of the minimum

At x = −4, the target x = 3 is seven units to your right. You can also test the slope: 2(x − 3) is negative, so subtracting it moves x right.

Notebook 02 · Lab

Make the steps visible.

Tune the optimizer, run it, and watch each guess move across L(x) = (x − 3)². Your controls and latest result are shared with your study partner.

Experiment controls

Choose a starting recipe

Change one variable at a time. Try η = 0.08, then η = 0.75. Keep the start and step count fixed. Which path settles, and which bounces?

Live trajectory

The valley at x = 3

Ready
Final x—
Final loss—
PatternRun to see

Notebook 03 · Reflect

Turn a run into learning.

Confidence is not a score—it is a signal for what to practice next. Leave a note your future self (or AI study partner) can act on.

Progress
